_doc: How she talks, waits and listens (2026-10-06). lib/crissa_talk.py reads this file, then <crissa home>/talk.json on top (Init writes that one), then the environment wins over both. 0 means no limit; null means leave the speaker's own default alone.

reply._tokens_doc: What the chat is asked for (round 15, 2026-10-12): max_tokens is a turn's reply budget; reading_tokens is a reading's budget per request ("go on" fetches the next part); context_tokens caps what is sent (system prompt + recent history + the turn, about 4 characters a token; the oldest history goes first). EAR_BRIDGE_MAX_TOKENS, EAR_BRIDGE_READING_TOKENS, EAR_BRIDGE_CONTEXT_TOKENS override. 0 = no cap of ours.

speak._piece_doc: A line longer than this is read as consecutive pieces of at most this many characters, each ending on a sentence, each its own line; nothing is dropped (round 14, 2026-10-12). 200-780; 0 = one line, cut at the voice's 800-character cap with a note.

turn._doc: When his turn ends and her mouth opens (round 17, 2026-10-13, the User: "yes cut the waits"; checkpoint round17-waits-20261013). end_s: the silence that closes his utterance in a conversation (the ear's hangover; was 2.0 s, 0.6 = two of its 0.3 s frames). speculate: her turn starts as his lands and is cancelled silently, then asked again with the whole utterance, if he goes on before her mouth opens. final_s: her mouth opens only after this much silence since he was last heard (2.0: a thinking pause of up to 1.5 s inside his sentence is not taken for his end even on a fast machine; the ear sees him start again 0.3-0.5 s late, so a pause about final_s long can still be answered early). gap_s: and this long after his turn reached the bridge (was 2.0 s). CRISSA_EAR_SPECULATE=0 (the 2.0 s hangover back, no speculation), CRISSA_SPEAK_GAP_S (2 = the old quiet), CRISSA_EAR_END_S, CRISSA_TURN_FINAL_S override.

barge._doc: What may cut her line while she speaks (round 18, 2026-10-13, the User: "Interrupt words only" and "Id like to talk with someone else while she speaks without interrupting her"; checkpoint round18-barge-words-20261013). words_only: only these words, or her name, cut her, straight from the ear's first look, with no voice check (false = round 17: any words of someone's). words: the interrupt words he approved, matched on word boundaries, case-insensitive, never when she is saying the same word herself; the ear also counts its measured spellings of them ("wansan" for one second, "nevermind"). Left out on purpose: okay, yes, no, sorry (every reply and reading has them; the ASR writes "No." and "Okay." for a cough or a key). name: her name and the spellings the ear has written for it (Chrissa, Chrisa, Krisa, ... and, over her line, Chris, Krista), when it calls her (after hey/hi/okay, or first or last in what was heard), never when she says it herself. names: more spellings of her name. side_talk: anything else said while she answers is not a cut and is never sent to her; it is shown on the Wall's log as room speech. CRISSA_BARGE_WORDS_ONLY=0 and CRISSA_SIDE_TALK=0 override.
